newsitem.title: UK: Colombia rating unlikely to be downgraded - Harf.
newsitem.headline: Colombia rating unlikely to be downgraded - Harf.

text.p: Foreign trade minister Morris Harf Meyer said Colombia's credit rating was unlikely to be downgraded despite recent political turbulence.
"I don't think that any of the indicators of our economic performance would indicate that (our rating) should be lowered or changed," Morris Harf Meyer told Reuters in an interview.
With a BBB- rating from Standard & Poor's, and BAA3 from Moody's, Colombia is the only Latin American nation besides Chile to have an investment grade rating.
But some analysts fear Standard & Poor's may alter its outlook to stable from positive due to perceptions that President Ernesto Samper's political standing has been weakened.

Although Samper himself has been exonerated of charges his election campaign was bankrolled by drug lords, vice-president Humberto de la Calle quit earlier this month citing Samper's alleged ties to drug kingpins and the government's deepening credibility gap. --Caroline Brothers, London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
